questions.question: Where should application.properties live in a Spring Boot project?
options: The project root, next to pom.xml
questions.explanation: Maven copies src/main/resources onto the classpath, where Spring Boot looks for application.properties.

questions.question: A file is saved at src/main/resources/static/css/site.css. Which URL serves it when the app runs on port 8080?
options: It is not served; you need a controller
questions.explanation: The static folder itself is not part of the URL; files are served at their path inside it.

questions.question: The main class is in com.crumbco.app and a @RestController is in com.crumbco.menu. The app starts, but GET /menu returns 404. Why?
options: Controllers must be in the same file as the main class
The menu package needs its own @SpringBootApplication
com.crumbco.menu is not below com.crumbco.app, so component scan never finds the controller
questions.explanation: Scanning starts at the main class's package and goes down; move the main class up to com.crumbco.

questions.question: Which folder's code is compiled and run during the build but NOT packaged into the final JAR?
questions.explanation: Test code under src/test/java is used by the build only and never ships with the app.

questions.question: A student saves server.port=9191 in src/main/java/application.properties, but the app still starts on port 8080. What is wrong?
options: server.port only works in YAML files
The file is in src/main/java, which Maven does not copy as a resource, so Spring Boot never sees it
Ports can only be changed on the command line
questions.explanation: Only files in src/main/resources are copied onto the classpath; move the file there.
